items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Write names of the various types of government.
items.answer:  The types of government are : Democracy (Direct and Representative - Parliamentary and Presidential), Monarchy (Absolute and Constitutional), Theocracy, Dictatorship, and Oligarchy.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which type of Government does India have? And why is that called that type?
items.answer:  India has a Parliamentary Democracy. It’s called this because the executive branch (Prime Minister and Council of Ministers) is drawn from and accountable to the legislature (Parliament), specifically the Lok Sabha.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: You read that an independent judiciary is present in all types of democracies. State any three reasons why you think it is important for the judiciary to be independent.
items.answer:  An independent judiciary is important because :

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Do you think democratic government is better than other forms of government? Why?
items.answer:  Yes, democratic government seems better because it is based on the will of the people, protects fundamental rights like equality and freedom, holds rulers accountable through elections, and aims for the welfare of all citizens, unlike dictatorships or absolute monarchies where power is unchecked and rights may be suppressed. items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What are possible hurdles in a democracy in achieving its values and ideals? How can they be overcome?
items.answer:  Hurdles include corruption, wealth disparity, excessive influence by elites (oligarchic tendencies), erosion of judicial independence, and manipulation of information. Overcoming them requires citizen vigilance, active participation, demanding accountability, strengthening independent institutions, promoting education, and ensuring press freedom.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Democracy is different from monarchy and dictatorship. Explain.
items.answer:  In a democracy, power originates from the people who elect their rulers, and rights are protected. In a monarchy, power is held by a hereditary king or queen. In a dictatorship, one person or a small group holds absolute, often unchecked, power, usually suppressing rights. MULT IPL E CHOICE QUESTIO 

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the primary role of a government in a country, according to Kautilya’s Arthashastra?

options.label: A
options.text: To expand its territory through constant war

options.label: B
options.text: To ensure the protection, order, and welfare

options.label: C
options.text: To accumulate maximum wealth for its ruler

options.label: D
options.text: To promote a single state religious belief

items.answer:  (B) To ensure the protection, order, and welfare Kautilya’s Arthashastra outlines a ruler’s duties as threefold : raksha (protection from external aggression), palana (maintenance of internal law and order), and yogakshema (safeguarding the people’s welfare).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which of these is NOT listed as a primary function of a modern government?

options.label: A
options.text: Maintaining law and order within society

items.answer:  (C) Controlling citizens’ personal daily choices NODIA CH 09: From the Rulers to the Ruled : Types of Governments Governments are responsible for law and order, international relations, and essential services. While they regulate certain aspects of life for public good, controlling all personal daily choices is not a primary function, especially in democracies.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does the term ‘democracy’ fundamentally mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Rule by a single, all-powerful leader chosen

options.label: B
options.text: Rule by the wealthiest citizens in society

options.label: C
options.text: Rule by the people, directly or through chosen

options.label: D
options.text: Rule by religious laws and spiritual leaders

items.answer:  (C) Rule by the people, directly or through chosen Democracy, derived from Greek words, essentially means ‘rule of the people’. This implies that the ultimate source of power and authority in a democratic system rests with the citizens of the country.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the ‘legislative’ function of a government?

options.label: A
options.text: The implementation of existing rules, laws

options.label: B
options.text: The creation of rules and new laws

options.label: C
options.text: Ensuring that all rules are followed

options.label: D
options.text: The adjudication of disputes between people

items.answer:  (B) The creation of rules and new laws The legislative function of government involves the process of making and enacting laws. This body, often called a parliament or congress, debates and passes legislation that serves as the framework for the country.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: According to Abraham Lincoln, democracy is a ‘government of the people, by the people, and for whom’?
items.answer:  (C) For the people Abraham Lincoln famously described democracy as a “government of the people, by the people, for the people”. This emphasizes that a democratic government should serve the interests and welfare of all its citizens.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the most fundamental difference between various types of government regarding their authority?

options.label: A
options.text: The color of their national flag

options.label: B
options.text: Who or what gives the government power

options.label: C
options.text: The geographical size of the whole country

options.label: D
options.text: The primary language spoken by officials

items.answer:  (B) Who or what gives the government power A key differentiator between government types is the source of their authority and power. For instance, in a democracy, power comes from the people; in a theocracy, it’s derived from religious beliefs.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is a ‘constitution’ in the context of a country’s governance?

options.label: A
options.text: A list of all historical rulers, kings

options.label: B
options.text: A book of fundamental rules and laws

options.label: C
options.text: A collection of national folk songs

options.label: D
options.text: An annual budget report for economy

items.answer:  (B) A book of fundamental rules and laws A constitution is a foundational document that outlines the basic principles, laws, and structures of a country’s government. It defines how the government works and the rights of citizens.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which of these is a fundamental principle of democracy ensuring every adult citizen’s right to vote?
items.answer:  (C) Universal adult franchise Universal adult franchise is a cornerstone of democracy, granting every adult citizen (above a certain age, regardless of gender, race, or wealth) the right to vote in elections and choose their representatives.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How does ‘direct democracy’ differ from ‘representative democracy’? none them choose

options.label: A
options.text: Direct has elected leaders; representative has

options.label: B
options.text: Direct has citizens rule; representative has

options.label: C
options.text: Direct is for big; representative for small

options.label: D
options.text: Direct has no laws; representative has many

items.answer:  (B) Direct has citizens rule; representative has them choose NODIA

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The fact that even in ancient Indian monarchies, kings were often expected to rule according to ‘rajadharma’ (king’s duty/righteousness) implies what? right them

options.label: B
options.text: There were ethical and moral expectations

options.label: C
options.text: Welfare of people was not a concern

items.answer:  (B) There were ethical and moral expectations them The concept of ‘rajadharma’ suggested that even kings were bound by certain duties and ethical principles, including ensuring the welfare of their subjects and ruling justly, rather than having completely arbitrary power.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How does the selection of leaders in a presidential democracy typically differ from that in a parliamentary democracy regarding the head of the executive? elects president elects legislature

options.label: C
options.text: Both directly elect their prime ministers

options.label: D
options.text: Neither involves any form of public vote

items.answer:  (B) Presidential elects president; parliamentary elects legislature In a presidential democracy, the people typically elect the president (head of executive) separately from the legislature. In a parliamentary democracy, people elect the legislature, and the executive (Prime Minister and ministers) is drawn from and accountable to the legislature.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which function of government is correctly paired with its description? laws rulers

options.label: B
options.text: Executive - Making and passing new policies

options.label: C
options.text: Judiciary - Interpreting laws and settling any

items.answer:  (C) Judiciary - Interpreting laws and settling any The judiciary is the branch of government responsible for interpreting laws, ensuring they are applied fairly, and adjudicating legal disputes, including determining if laws have been broken and what punishments are appropriate.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A country’s constitution ensures that all adult citizens can vote, fundamental rights like freedom of speech are protected, and the courts can operate without government interference. These features are most characteristic of which type of government, ideally?
items.answer:  (C) A democratic government form Universal adult franchise, protection of fundamental rights, and an independent judiciary are core principles and characteristics of a democratic system of government, designed to ensure citizen participation and protect liberties.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which of these is NOT a fundamental principle typically associated with a functioning democracy? posts election

options.label: A
options.text: Equality before the law for all citizens

options.label: B
options.text: Freedom of expression and making choices

items.answer:  (C) Hereditary succession for all government posts Democracies emphasize equality, freedom, and representative participation through elections. Hereditary succession for government positions is characteristic of monarchies, not democracies where leaders are chosen by the people or their representatives.

options.label: B

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The Uttaramerur inscriptions from the Chola period provide details about the election of members to what local administrative body?

options.label: A
options.text: The royal council of state ministers

options.label: C
options.text: The village sabha or the assembly

items.answer:  (C) The village sabha or the assembly The 10th-century Uttaramerur inscriptions in Tamil Nadu offer remarkable details about the functioning of local self-government during the Chola period, including the process for electing members to the village assembly (sabha).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which of these was NOT a feature of the election process described in the Uttaramerur inscriptions?

options.label: A
options.text: Use of sealed ballot boxes for voting

options.label: C
options.text: Voting rights for all adult men, women

items.answer:  (C) Voting rights for all adult men, women The Uttaramerur inscriptions detail aspects like ballot boxes, member qualifications, and dismissal for corruption. However, voting rights in such ancient systems were often limited and not universally extended to all adults as in modern democracies.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which type of government is correctly matched with its defining characteristic? new monarch control

options.label: A
options.text: Direct Democracy - Ruled by a hereditary

options.label: B
options.text: Theocracy - Power held by a small elite group

options.label: D
options.text: Oligarchy - All citizens participate in decisions

items.answer:  (C) Absolute Monarchy - Monarch has complete control An absolute monarchy is a form of government where the monarch (king or queen) holds supreme, autocratic authority, and their power is not restricted by a constitution or laws.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which country is provided as an example of an absolute monarchy where the king holds all power?
items.answer:  (B) Saudi Arabia Saudi Arabia is cited as an example of an absolute monarchy, where the king possesses ultimate governing authority, and governance is often based on Islamic law.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How does a ‘constitutional monarchy’ like the United Kingdom differ from an ‘absolute monarchy’? one nominal real

options.label: A
options.text: Constitutional has no monarch; absolute has

options.label: D
options.text: Both have monarchs with identical powers

items.answer:  (C) Constitutional monarch has nominal; absolute real In an absolute monarchy, the monarch wields complete power. In a constitutional monarchy like the UK, the monarch is the head of state but has largely ceremonial or nominal powers, with actual governing power resting with an elected parliament and prime minister.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which country is given as an example of a place where some forms of direct democracy are followed?
items.answer:  (C) Switzerland Switzerland is often cited as an example of a country that incorporates elements of direct democracy into its political system, allowing citizens to vote directly on specific policies and laws through referendums.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does ‘accountability’ mean in a representative democracy?

options.label: A
options.text: The government can act without any public

options.label: B
options.text: The government is answerable to the people

options.label: C
options.text: Representatives hold their positions for life

items.answer:  (B) The government is answerable to the people Accountability in a representative democracy means that the elected government and its officials are responsible and answerable to the citizens who elected them for their actions and decisions.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In India, general elections to the Lok Sabha are typically held at what regular interval?
items.answer:  (C) Every five years India follows a system where general elections to the Lok Sabha (the Lower House of Parliament) are held every five years. This ensures regular opportunities for citizens to choose their representatives.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In a parliamentary democracy like India, if the Council of Ministers loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, what is the typical consequence? power

options.label: A
options.text: The ministers continue working with more

options.label: B
options.text: The President takes over all executive power

options.label: C
options.text: The ministers must resign from their posts

options.label: D
options.text: The Lok Sabha is dissolved permanently

items.answer:  (C) The ministers must resign from their posts In a parliamentary system, the executive (Council of Ministers) is accountable to the legislature (Lok Sabha). If they lose the confidence of the Lok Sabha, they are typically required to resign, leading to a new government formation.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the ‘executive’ branch of government primarily responsible for?

options.label: A
options.text: Making and passing all new national laws

items.answer:  (C) Implementing laws and administering country The executive branch of government is responsible for implementing and enforcing the laws made by the legislature, as well as managing the day-to- day administration of the country.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In most democratic countries, the legislature, responsible for making laws, is known by different names; in India, it is called the _____.
items.answer:  (C) Parliament The legislature in India, which is the supreme law- making body, is known as the Parliament. It consists of two houses : the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments

options.label: D

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In ancient Greece, some city-states were ruled by aristocratic families. This form of governance would be classified as what?
items.answer:  (C) An oligarchy Rule by a small group of aristocratic (noble and wealthy) families, as seen in some ancient Greek city-states, is a classic example of an oligarchy, where power is concentrated in the hands of a privileged few.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Why is democracy generally considered a better form of government than others like dictatorship or absolute monarchy?

options.label: B
options.text: It better protects people’s choices, rights

options.label: C
options.text: It leads to more economic equality

options.label: D
options.text: It guarantees absence of any corruption

items.answer:  (B) It better protects people’s choices, rights Democracy is often preferred because it ideally allows people to lead their lives with freedom, make their own choices, express themselves, and hold their government accountable for protecting their rights.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A country’s government is structured such that the head of state is a monarch who inherited the position, but real governing power lies with an elected parliament and a prime minister who is accountable to it. This country has which form of government system?

options.label: A
options.text: An absolute monarchy with all power

items.answer:  (C) A constitutional monarchy This describes a constitutional monarchy, where the monarch’s role is largely ceremonial, and actual political power is exercised by an elected legislature and an executive (Prime Minister and cabinet) accountable to it.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The early Indian mahajanapada of Vajji, particularly the Lichchhavi clan, practiced collective decision-making and is often cited as an example of an early _____.
items.answer:  (B) republic The Vajji confederacy, especially the Lichchhavis, had a system where leaders were chosen, and decisions were made collectively by an assembly, rather than by a hereditary monarch. This has led scholars to describe them as early republics.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does the term ‘sovereign’ mean in the context of a country’s government? external

options.label: A
options.text: The government is directly elected by people

options.label: B
options.text: The country’s power is independent of

options.label: C
options.text: The monarch has only ceremonial duties

options.label: D
options.text: The military has ultimate control over state

items.answer:  (B) The country’s power is independent of external ‘Sovereign’ indicates that a country’s government has supreme and independent authority within its own territory, free from external control or influence in its decision-making processes.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The Romani people, who faced persecution under Hitler, are believed by scholars to have originated from which country based on linguistic and cultural characteristics?
items.answer:  (C) India Linguistic and cultural studies suggest that the Romani people, often historically referred to as Gypsies, originated in India before migrating to various parts of the world, including Europe. NODIA

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which country is mentioned as having a unique political system combining elements of theocratic and democratic governance, with a Supreme Leader?
items.answer:  (C) Iran today Iran’s political system is described as a unique combination of theocratic elements (with a Supreme Leader holding ultimate authority based on Islamic principles) and democratic features (like an elected president and parliament).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A country is ruled by one person who seized power by force, is not bound by any constitution, and suppresses all opposition. This form of government is best described as a/an :
items.answer:  (C) Dictatorship This description matches a dictatorship, where a single leader or a small group holds absolute power, often obtained and maintained by force, without constitutional limitations, and typically suppressing dissent and opposition.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Assertion : In India’s parliamentary democracy, the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers are part of the legislature. Reason (R) : The executive in a parliamentary system is accountable to the legislature and requires its confidence. explanation of A. correct explanation of A.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer:  (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. In India’s parliamentary system, the executive (Prime Minister and ministers) are indeed members of the Parliament (legislature). This structure ensures their accountability to the legislature, as they must maintain its confidence to remain in power.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A dictatorship often involves suppression of fundamental rights for all. Which of the above statements is/are correct about this?
items.answer:  (A) 3 only In direct democracy, citizens make laws directly, not through representatives. An absolute monarch’s power is not constitutionally limited. Dictatorships often suppress rights.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does the ‘judicial function’ of government primarily involve?

options.label: A
options.text: Creating new laws for the entire country

options.label: B
options.text: Implementing the policies decided by leaders

options.label: C
options.text: Ensuring rules are followed, settling disputes

items.answer:  (C) Ensuring rules are followed, settling disputes The judicial function of government is concerned with interpreting laws, ensuring they are upheld, resolving legal disputes, and administering justice when laws are broken.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How does the source of authority in a democracy like India differ from that in a theocracy? religious wealth people foreign
items.answer:  (A) Democracy from people; theocracy from religious In a democracy such as India, the ultimate source of governmental authority is the people. In a theocracy, authority is derived from religious beliefs and institutions, with governance based on religious law.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The story of King Chandrapida and the cobbler from Kalhana’s Rajatarangini illustrates the king’s commitment to _____, even towards a lowly subject.
items.answer:  (C) dharma (justice) The narrative highlights King Chandrapida’s adherence to dharma (righteousness and justice) by respecting the cobbler’s rights and feelings regarding his hut, even when it inconvenienced the king’s plans, showing fairness.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Why is an independent judiciary considered a crucial component of a healthy democracy?

options.label: A
options.text: It helps the executive implement laws faster

options.label: B
options.text: It ensures fundamental rights are protected

options.label: C
options.text: It allows legislature to pass any laws

options.label: D
options.text: It makes government decisions less transparent

items.answer:  (B) It ensures fundamental rights are protected An independent judiciary is vital in a democracy because it acts as a guardian of the constitution and citizens’ fundamental rights. It ensures that both the government and individuals act within the bounds of the law.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A country’s laws are all based on sacred religious texts, and the head of state is also the supreme religious leader, whose authority is considered divinely ordained. This system of government is best described as a/an :

options.label: A
options.text: Oligarchy based on business interests only

items.answer:  (D) Theocracy ruled by religious principles This scenario describes a theocracy, where governance is based on religious laws and principles, and religious leaders often hold ultimate political authority, believed to be divinely sanctioned.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In India, the three organs of government— Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary—are expected to work independently due to the principle of _____ of Power.
items.answer:  (C) Separation The principle of Separation of Powers advocates for the distinct and independent functioning of the legislative (law-making), executive (law- implementing), and judicial (law-interpreting) branches of government to prevent any single branch from becoming overly powerful.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The story of Shane in North Korea, who faces strict rules about haircuts, clothing, and internet access, and lives under constant government surveillance, illustrates life under what type of regime?

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A country holds regular, free, and fair elections where all adult citizens have the right to vote for their leaders. The elected government is accountable to the people, and fundamental rights are protected by an independent judiciary. This country operates under which system of government?
items.answer:  (B) A representative democracy These features – regular free elections, universal adult suffrage, accountable government, protection of fundamental rights, and an independent judiciary – are the hallmarks of a representative democracy.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments

items.answer:  (C) Saudi Arabia - Constitutional Monarchy Saudi Arabia is cited as an example of an absolute monarchy, where the king holds complete power. The United Kingdom is given as an example of a constitutional monarchy.

options.label: D
options.text: Lower House deals with foreign; Upper House

items.answer:  (B) Lower House is more powerful; Upper House less In many bicameral (two-house) legislatures, the Lower House, which is typically directly elected by the people, often holds more power, particularly in financial matters and government formation, compared to the Upper House.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which form of government is described as having a ruler whose power is inherited and who is not limited by a constitution?
items.answer:  (C) Absolute Monarchy with its king An absolute monarchy is characterized by a ruler (monarch) who inherits their position and exercises supreme, unrestricted power, not bound by a constitution or other legal limitations.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A political commentator observes that in a particular democracy, a very small group of extremely wealthy business leaders seems to exert undue influence over government policies and decisions, benefiting their own interests disproportionately. This situation shows signs of the democracy potentially tending towards what?
items.answer:  (B) An oligarchy of the elites When a small, powerful, and often wealthy elite group wields excessive influence over government, potentially to the detriment of broader public interest, it signals a drift towards oligarchy, even within a formally democratic system.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which of these is NOT a reason why democracy is generally valued over other forms of government?

options.label: A
options.text: It allows people to choose their government

options.label: B
options.text: It holds the government accountable to citizen

options.label: C
options.text: It guarantees absence of all social issues

options.label: D
options.text: It aims for well-being of all its people

items.answer:  (C) It guarantees absence of all social issues While democracy strives to address societal problems and protect rights, it does not guarantee the complete absence of all social issues or challenges. It provides a framework for addressing them.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the term for the official, often violent, persecution and extermination of Jews by Nazi Germany under Adolf Hitler?
items.answer:  (C) The Holocaust The Holocaust was the systematic, state- sponsored persecution and genocide of six million Jews by the Nazi regime and its collaborators during World War II.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does the term ‘adjudicating’ mean in a legal or governmental context?

options.label: A
options.text: The process of creating and passing laws

options.label: B
options.text: The act of enforcing laws on population

options.label: C
options.text: Judging a case or dispute officially

options.label: D
options.text: The system of collecting taxes from all

items.answer:  (C) Judging a case or dispute officially Adjudicating refers to the formal process of making an official decision or judgment on a disputed matter, typically by a court or a judge, after hearing evidence and arguments from all sides involved.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Assertion (A) : The Uttaramerur inscriptions indicate that ancient Indian villages had systems for electing local administrative members. Reason (R) : These inscriptions show that such local bodies had no real power and were fully controlled by the king. explanation of A. correct explanation of A.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer:  (C) A is true, but R is false The Uttaramerur inscriptions do provide evidence of elections for local village sabhas (assemblies) in the Chola period. However, these local bodies had defined responsibilities and could even dismiss members for corruption, suggesting a degree of autonomy, not complete royal control.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Fundamental rights are optional guidelines for the government to follow. Which of the above statements is/are correct in that context?
items.answer:  (A) 2 only Universal adult franchise means all adults (above a certain age) can vote. Separation of powers is indeed about checks and balances. Fundamental rights are generally enforceable protections for citizens, not optional guidelines.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In a _____ democracy, the executive branch works independently of the legislature, and the president is often elected directly by the people.
items.answer:  (C) presidential In a presidential democracy, there is a clear separation between the executive (headed by the president) and the legislature. The president is usually elected independently by the people and does not depend on the legislature’s confidence to hold office.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is a ‘representative’ in the context of democratic governance?

options.label: A
options.text: A citizen who directly makes all laws

options.label: B
options.text: A person chosen to act on behalf

options.label: C
options.text: An unelected official with absolute power

options.label: D
options.text: A monarch who inherits their position

items.answer:  (B) A person chosen to act on behalf A representative is an individual selected or elected by a group of people (constituents) to act, speak, or make decisions on their behalf, typically within a legislative body or other governing institution.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In which century did women in Switzerland gain the right to vote in federal elections?
items.answer:  (C) 20th century Switzerland, despite its democratic traditions, granted women the right to vote in federal elections relatively late, in 1971, which falls within the 20th century.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The existence of different forms of democratic governments (e.g., parliamentary vs. presidential) around the world primarily illustrates what? suit

options.label: A
options.text: That democracy is a flawed and failing system

options.label: B
options.text: That countries adapt democratic principles to

options.label: C
options.text: That only one specific model of democracy

options.label: D
options.text: That democracy is only suitable for small

items.answer:  (B) That countries adapt democratic principles to suit The variations in democratic structures, such as parliamentary and presidential systems, show that while core democratic principles are shared, countries often adapt these principles and design their governmental frameworks to fit their unique historical, cultural, and societal contexts. NODIA CH 09: From the Rulers to the Ruled : Types of Governments challenges represent deviations from or failures to achieve democratic ideals.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The judiciary ensures that laws are followed by citizens and government. Which of the above statements is/are correct generally?
items.answer:  (A) 3 only The legislature makes laws; the executive implements them. In a presidential system, the president (executive) is separate from the legislature. The judiciary indeed interprets laws and ensures they are followed.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata contains Bhishma’s teachings to Yudhisthira on good governance, justice, and the moral responsibilities of a _____.
items.answer:  (C) raja (king) In the Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata, the wise elder Bhishma imparts extensive teachings to Yudhisthira on the principles of rajadharma, which encompasses good governance, justice, and the ethical duties of a raja (king).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does “Universal Adult Franchise” guarantee in a democracy?

options.label: A
options.text: Free education for all adult citizens

options.label: B
options.text: The right of every adult citizen to vote

options.label: D
options.text: Freedom of speech for all adults only

items.answer:  (B) The right of every adult citizen to vote Universal Adult Franchise is a democratic principle that grants the right to vote to all adult citizens of a country, typically without discrimination based on race, sex, belief, or social status (though age restrictions apply).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which ancient Indian text, composed by Kautilya, discusses statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy in detail?
items.answer:  (C) Arthashastra The Arthashastra, attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya), is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, political science, economic policy, and military strategy, offering comprehensive guidance on governance and administration.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The existence of an ‘Upper House’ and a ‘Lower House’ in the legislature of many democracies signifies what kind of legislative structure?
items.answer:  (B) A bicameral (two-house) system mainly A legislature composed of two separate assemblies, chambers, or houses (typically an Upper House and a Lower House) is known as a bicameral system. This structure is common in many democratic countries, including India and the USA.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How does the power of the monarch in an absolute monarchy like Saudi Arabia compare to that of the monarch in a constitutional monarchy like the UK? limited

options.label: A
options.text: Both have equally unlimited governing powers

options.label: B
options.text: Saudi monarch has real; UK monarch nominal

options.label: C
options.text: UK monarch has absolute; Saudi monarch

options.label: D
options.text: Neither has any significant political power

items.answer:  (B) Saudi monarch has real; UK monarch nominal In an absolute monarchy like Saudi Arabia, the monarch holds virtually all governing power. In a constitutional monarchy like the UK, the monarch’s powers are largely ceremonial and symbolic, with real political authority vested in elected officials. Click Here to Buy book on Amazon

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which description correctly defines ‘Fundamental Rights’ in a democracy?

options.label: A
options.text: Optional duties citizens may choose to perform

options.label: B
options.text: Basic protected rights for all citizens

options.label: C
options.text: Privileges granted only to government workers

items.answer:  (B) Basic protected rights for all citizens Fundamental Rights are a set of basic human rights guaranteed to all citizens in a democracy, protected by the constitution, such as the right to equality, freedom, and against exploitation.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A government body is responsible for ensuring that new laws passed by the parliament align with the country’s constitution and for settling legal arguments about these laws. This body is performing which essential function of government?
items.answer:  (C) The judicial (law-interpreting) function Interpreting laws, ensuring their constitutionality, and resolving legal disputes are the primary responsibilities of the judicial branch of government. This function is crucial for upholding the rule of law.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a dictatorship?

options.label: A
options.text: Absolute power held by one person or group

options.label: B
options.text: Limitations imposed by a strong constitution

options.label: D
options.text: Absence of free and fair electoral choice

items.answer:  (B) Limitations imposed by a strong constitution Dictatorships are defined by the ruler(s) possessing absolute power without limitations from a constitution or law. They often involve suppression of opposition and the absence of genuine democratic processes.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The term ‘rajadharma’ in ancient India referred to the duties and righteous conduct expected of whom?
items.answer:  (C) Kings or rulers ‘Rajadharma’ pertains to the set of duties, responsibilities, and ethical principles that a king or ruler was expected to follow in ancient Indian political thought, emphasizing just governance and the welfare of subjects.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is a ‘caricature’ as shown in the figures of Adolf Hitler and Idi Amin?

options.label: A
options.text: A realistic, photographic portrait of person

options.label: B
options.text: A formal statue erected in their honor

options.label: C
options.text: A drawing exaggerating features for humor

options.label: D
options.text: An official document signed by the leader

items.answer:  (C) A drawing exaggerating features for humor A caricature is a rendered image showing the features of its subject in a simplified or exaggerated way, often for satirical or humorous effect, as seen with the depictions of Hitler and Idi Amin.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the primary difference in how the head of the executive (e.g., President or Prime Minister) usually attains power in a democracy versus an absolute monarchy? inheritance election

options.label: B
options.text: Democracy via inheritance; monarchy via an

options.label: C
options.text: Both are appointed by religious leadership

options.label: D
options.text: Both seize power through military action

items.answer:  (A) Democracy via election; monarchy via inheritance In most democracies, the head of the executive is chosen through some form of election by the people or their representatives. In absolute monarchies, the monarch typically inherits their position through familial succession.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The ancient Lichchhavi clan, known for its republican traditions, was part of the larger _____ mahajanapada.
items.answer:  (C) Vajji (Vriji) The Lichchhavis were a prominent clan within the Vajji (or Vriji) mahajanapada, which was NODIA CH 09: From the Rulers to the Ruled : Types of Governments a confederacy of clans known for its republican or oligarchic form of governance, distinct from contemporary monarchies.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The idea that “the government is accountable to the people who have elected them” is a core principle of which system?
items.answer:  (B) Representative Democracy Accountability to the electorate is a fundamental tenet of representative democracy, where elected officials are responsible for their actions and decisions to the citizens who vested them with power through elections.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A citizen in a country feels their fundamental right to equality has been violated by a new government policy. In a functioning democracy with an independent judiciary, what recourse does this citizen ideally have to seek justice?

options.label: A
options.text: They must accept the policy without question

options.label: B
options.text: They can appeal directly to a foreign nation

options.label: C
options.text: They can approach the courts for a review

options.label: D
options.text: They should organize a protest to stop it

items.answer:  (C) They can approach the courts for a review. In a democracy with an independent judiciary, citizens whose fundamental rights are violated can seek redress by approaching the courts. The judiciary has the power to review government actions and policies to ensure they align with the constitution and protect citizens’ rights. MAT CHING TYPE QUESTION 

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: According to Kautilya, what are the three-fold duties of a ruler in internal administration?
items.answer:  Raksha (protection), Palana (law and order), and Yogakshema (welfare).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Name one essential function of any government.
items.answer:  Maintain law and order/Ensure peace/security/ Manage foreign relations/National defence/ Deliver essential services/Manage economy/Work for people’s welfare (any one).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What form of government does India have?
items.answer:  Democratic government (specifically, Parliamentary Democracy).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does ‘democracy’ literally mean?
items.answer:  Rule of the people.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In a democracy, who is the ultimate source of power and authority?
items.answer:  The people of the country.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the function of government concerned with making rules or laws called?
items.answer:  Legislative function.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the function of government concerned with implementing rules and administration called?
items.answer:  Executive function.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the function of government concerned with ensuring rules are followed and interpreted called?
items.answer:  Judicial function.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Who famously described democracy as ‘government of the people, by the people, for the people’?
items.answer:  Abraham Lincoln.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the book containing the fundamental rules of a country often called?
items.answer:  Constitution.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What principle ensures that every person has the right to be treated equally in a democracy?
items.answer:  Equality.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What principle grants every adult citizen the right to vote in elections?
items.answer:  Universal adult franchise.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which organ of government ensures that citizens’ fundamental rights are protected?
items.answer:  Independent judiciary.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In which country mentioned did women get the right to vote only in 1971?
items.answer:  Switzerland.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What type of democracy involves all citizens participating directly in decision-making?
items.answer:  Direct democracy.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the most common form of democracy where people elect representatives?
items.answer:  Representative democracy.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does ‘accountability’ mean in a democracy?
items.answer:  The government is answerable to the people who elected them.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: In India, the Parliament (Legislature) consists of the Lok Sabha and which other house?
items.answer:  Rajya Sabha (Upper House). Click Here to Buy book on Flipkart

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Considering Shane’s story in North Korea, analyse how the lack of democratic principles impacts citizens’ daily lives and awareness.
items.answer:  Lack of democracy severely curtails personal freedom (restricted choices in appearance, movement, information access via internet). Compulsory service and constant surveillance create an environment of fear and conformity. Restricted information prevents awareness of alternatives or external perspectives, reinforcing state control over citizens’ lives and thoughts.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Analyse the potential long-term consequences for a society ruled by a dictator like Hitler or Idi Amin.
items.answer:  Dictatorships often lead to severe human rights abuses (mass killings, persecution of minorities like Jews/Roma under Hitler, expulsion/killing of ethnic groups under Amin), suppression of freedoms, economic mismanagement or exploitation, international isolation, and devastating wars (WWII under Hitler), leaving deep, lasting scars on society.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Why is the ‘separation of powers’ considered a vital mechanism for preventing tyranny or abuse of power in a democracy?
items.answer:  By dividing governmental functions (legislative, executive, judicial) among independent branches, separation of powers creates checks and balances. No single branch can accumulate absolute authority. Each branch can limit the power of the others, preventing tyranny and safeguarding citizens’ liberties from potential government overreach.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Using Table given below, analyse why democracy is often associated with promoting the “Wellbeing and Prosperity of all citizens” more than other forms of government shown. Characteristics Democracy Dictatorship Absolute Monarchy Oligarchy Universal Adult Franchise Yes No No No Equality amongst citizens Freedom of speech Separation of powers Wellbeing and Prosperity of all citizens
items.answer:  Democracies ideally ensure equality, allowing all citizens opportunities. Freedom of speech allows needs to be voiced. Accountability via elections pressures governments to address citizens’ welfare. Other forms often prioritize the rulers (monarchy, dictatorship) or a small group (oligarchy), lacking mechanisms to ensure the well-being of the entire populace.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Evaluate the challenges faced in transitioning from a non-democratic system (like monarchy or colonial rule) to a stable democracy, considering India’s experience.
items.answer:  Challenges include establishing democratic institutions (parliament, judiciary), ensuring fair elections (universal franchise), overcoming deep social inequalities (caste, poverty), educating citizens about rights/responsibilities, preventing corruption, and fostering national unity amidst diversity. India successfully established institutions but continues to grapple with many of these socio-economic challenges.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: “Vigilant citizens are the ultimate safeguard of democracy.” Analyse the meaning and importance of this statement, considering the hurdles.
items.answer:  This means democracy’s health depends on citizens actively participating, staying informed, questioning authority, and defending rights. Hurdles like corruption, misinformation, or elite capture can undermine democracy. Vigilant citizens who hold power accountable, demand transparency, and participate thoughtfully are crucial to counteracting these threats and preserving democratic ideals. CASE BASED QUESTIO 

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the main limitation of direct democracy, especially in large countries?
items.answer:  Direct democracy, where all citizens vote on all issues, becomes very difficult and impractical to manage in large populations, making timely decision-making and effective implementation nearly impossible.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How are governments held accountable to the people in a representative democracy?
items.answer:  Governments are held accountable primarily through regular elections, where people can choose to re-elect representatives or vote them out if they are unsatisfied with their performance or policies.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Explain the key difference between parliamentary and presidential forms of democracy regarding the executive.
items.answer:  In parliamentary democracy (like India), the executive (Prime Minister/ministers) is part of and accountable to the legislature. In presidential democracy (like USA), the executive (President) is elected separately and works independently of the legislature.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does ‘separation of powers’ mean in the context of government organs?
items.answer:  Separation of powers means the legislative (law- making), executive (law-implementing), and judicial (law-interpreting) branches of government operate independently, preventing any one branch from becoming too powerful.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How did the ancient Lichchhavi clan (part of Vajji) demonstrate republican principles?
items.answer:  The Lichchhavis practiced collective decision- making in assemblies, chose leaders based on merit (not just birth), potentially used elections, and focused on people’s welfare, reflecting early republican ideals.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What do the Uttaramerur inscriptions reveal about local governance in the Chola period?
items.answer:  They reveal a sophisticated system of village self-governance (sabha) with detailed procedures for electing members (using ballots), defining qualifications and duties, and even rules for removing corrupt members.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What limitations existed in ancient Greek republics regarding citizen participation?
items.answer:  While pioneering republican ideas, participation was often limited. In some areas, only free men could vote, excluding women, workers, and slaves. In others, only a small, privileged group held decision-making power.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Explain the concept of ‘rajadharma’ as applied to ancient Indian kings.
items.answer:  Rajadharma meant that a king’s rule was bound by dharma (righteous duty/law). He was expected to rule justly, ensure the welfare of all subjects, and seek wise counsel, rather than exercising absolute, arbitrary power.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is the difference between an absolute monarchy and a constitutional monarchy? Give examples.
items.answer:  In an absolute monarchy (e.g., Saudi Arabia), the monarch holds supreme, often unlimited power. In a constitutional monarchy (e.g., UK), the monarch is a head of state with limited/ceremonial powers defined by a constitution, while real power lies with an elected parliament/government.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Describe the main characteristic of a theocracy.
items.answer:  A theocracy is a form of government where rule is based on religious law, and religious leaders hold significant political authority, often claiming divine guidance. Iran is given as a key example.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Briefly describe the conditions in North Korea based on Shane’s story.
items.answer:  Conditions include compulsory military service, strict government control over personal appearance (hair, clothes), restricted access to outside information (internet), close surveillance, and lack of personal freedom or choice.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Explain what an oligarchy is.
items.answer:  An oligarchy is a form of government where power rests with a small, elite group, often distinguished by wealth, family ties, or military control, who make decisions for the whole society.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: According to the comparison table, which form(s) of government typically lack universal adult franchise? Characteristics Democracy Dictatorship Absolute Monarchy Oligarchy Universal Adult Franchise Yes No No No Equality amongst citizens Freedom of speech Separation of powers Wellbeing and Prosperity of all citizens
items.answer:  Dictatorship, absolute monarchy, and oligarchy typically lack universal adult franchise, as power is not derived from the broad population’s vote.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Why is democracy considered preferable by many compared to other forms like dictatorship or monarchy?
items.answer:  Democracy is preferred because it upholds principles like equality, freedom, and citizen participation (voting). Governments are accountable to the people, rights are protected, and power isn’t concentrated arbitrarily.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: List two potential problems or challenges that even democratic governments can face.
items.answer:  Democracies can face challenges like corruption, wealth disparity influencing politics, manipulation of information, erosion of judicial independence, or excessive control by powerful groups.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How can citizens help keep democracy strong?
items.answer:  Citizens can stay informed, participate actively (voting, discussions), hold elected officials accountable, protect fundamental rights, respect diverse opinions, and remain vigilant against threats like corruption or misinformation.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does it mean for a country to be ‘sovereign’?
items.answer:  A sovereign country possesses supreme and independent power or authority over its own territory, free from external control or influence in its governance. LONG ANSWER QUESTIO 

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Analyse the three functions of government (legislative, executive, judicial) using the example of the school committee analogy.
items.answer:  Making rules for school activities (timetables, sports) is the legislative function. Implementing these rules and managing tasks (serving meals, organizing assembly) is the executive function. Ensuring students follow rules and perhaps resolving disputes related to them represents the judicial function, all carried out by the student committee.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Compare and contrast direct democracy and representative democracy. Why is representative democracy more common in large, modern nations?
items.answer:  Direct democracy involves all citizens voting on all laws/decisions. Representative democracy involves citizens electing officials to make decisions on their behalf. Direct democracy is impractical for large populations due to logistical challenges in participation and decision-making, making representative systems more feasible for modern nation-states. Downloaded from www.pdf.tube CH 09: From the Rulers to the Ruled : Types of Governments

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Analyse the relationship between the executive and legislature in a parliamentary democracy (like India) versus a presidential democracy (like USA).
items.answer:  In parliamentary systems, the executive (PM, ministers) emerges from and is accountable to the legislature (must maintain its confidence). In presidential systems, the executive (President) is elected separately and functions independently of the legislature, leading to a stricter separation of powers between the two branches.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Evaluate the significance of the Uttaramerur inscriptions in understanding democratic traditions in ancient India. What are their limitations?
items.answer:  These inscriptions are highly significant, providing concrete evidence of sophisticated local self-governance with democratic elements like elections (ballots), specific qualifications, and accountability (removal for corruption) in Chola times. Limitations include it being a local example; we don’t know how widespread or long- lasting this specific system was.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: “The concept of Rajadharma in ancient India acted as a check on monarchical power.” Analyse this statement.
items.answer:  Rajadharma prescribed that a king’s actions must align with righteousness and prioritize subjects’ welfare. While not a formal constitution, this principle created a moral and ethical framework limiting arbitrary rule. Kings ignoring dharma risked losing legitimacy and support, acting as an ideological check on absolute power.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Compare the source of authority and limitations on power in an absolute monarchy versus a dictatorship.
items.answer:  In absolute monarchy, authority often derives from tradition (heredity) and sometimes divine right, with theoretical limits imposed by religious law or custom (like Rajadharma). In dictatorship, authority usually stems from force (military coup, revolution), with power being absolute and practically unlimited by law or constitution, often maintained through repression.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Analyse the key features that distinguish a theocracy from other forms of government like democracy or monarchy.
items.answer:  Theocracy’s defining feature is its basis in religious law and the prominent role of religious leaders in governance, often holding ultimate authority (like Iran’s Supreme Leader). Unlike democracy (people’s sovereignty) or monarchy (hereditary rule), ultimate authority stems from religious doctrine and interpretation by clerical figures.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: “Even democracies can exhibit oligarchic tendencies.” Analyse how this might happen, referring to the cartoon (Fig.) or modern examples.
items.answer:  Oligarchic tendencies emerge when wealth or influence becomes concentrated, allowing a small elite (rich industrialists, powerful lobbyists, entrenched politicians – symbolized by the large figures dominating the Senate in the cartoon) to exert disproportionate control over policy- making, overriding the broader public interest despite democratic structures being formally in place.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Evaluate the importance of fundamental rights (like freedom of speech, equality) in ensuring a functional democracy.
items.answer:  Fundamental rights are crucial. Freedom of speech allows open debate and criticism of government. Equality ensures all citizens can participate and are treated fairly by law. Protecting these rights prevents suppression of dissent, ensures broad participation, and holds the government accountable, making democracy meaningful and functional. NODIA

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What principle ensures that the Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary work independently?
items.answer:  Separation of Power.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Name one ancient Indian mahajanapada that functioned as an early republic (gana/sangha).
items.answer:  Vajji (or Vrijji)/Malla (any one).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Which Chola-era inscriptions give details about village sabha elections?
items.answer:  Uttaramerur inscriptions.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What type of government is ruled by a king or queen, usually inheriting the position?
items.answer:  Monarchy.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What type of government is ruled based on religious laws and by religious leaders?
items.answer:  Theocracy.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What type of government involves one person or a small group holding absolute, unlimited power?
items.answer:  Dictatorship.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What type of government involves rule by a small, powerful, often wealthy group?
items.answer:  Oligarchy. SSHORT Answer QUESTIO 

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: List three key roles or functions performed by modern governments.
items.answer:  Governments maintain law and order, provide essential services like education and healthcare, manage the economy, ensure national defense, and manage relations with other countries.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Using the school committee example, explain why representative democracy is often preferred over direct participation in large groups.
items.answer:  Just as having every student on a committee makes decision-making difficult, direct participation by all citizens in large countries is impractical. Electing representatives allows for efficient governance while still reflecting the people’s will.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Explain the three main functions of government : legislative, executive, and judicial.
items.answer:  The legislative function involves making laws. The executive function involves implementing those laws and running the administration. The judicial function involves interpreting laws and ensuring they are followed, resolving disputes.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What are four key aspects that differentiate various forms of government?
items.answer:  Differences arise from : who holds ultimate authority, how the government is formed, the structure/parts of government and their roles, and the government’s goals/values (e.g., welfare for all vs few).

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does ‘equality’ mean as a fundamental principle of democracy?
items.answer:  Equality in democracy means every person has the right to equal treatment, equal access to facilities (education, health), and is considered equal before the law, regardless of background.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Explain the importance of ‘universal adult franchise’ in a representative democracy.
items.answer:  Universal adult franchise ensures that all adult citizens, regardless of gender, race, class, etc., have the equal right to vote and choose their representatives, forming the basis of popular sovereignty.

AAns  An independent judiciary protects citizens’ fundamental rights from violation by the state Click Here to Buy book on Amazon CH 09: From the Rulers to the Ruled : Types of Governments (ii) How would a decision likely be reached in this scenario? (iii) Compare how this decision-making process differs from how a similar decision might be made in a typical monarchy of that era.
items.answer:  (i) Vajji’s republican system (gana/sangha) featured collective decision-making in assemblies (sabha) where representatives from different groups could voice concerns and debate important issues like taxation and war. (ii) A decision would likely be reached through further discussion among the representatives in the sabha, possibly followed by a vote to determine the majority opinion on whether to increase taxes. (iii) In a typical monarchy, the king would likely make the final decision, perhaps after consulting ministers or elders, but without necessarily requiring a formal debate or vote among representatives of different groups as in the Vajji sabha.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: A modern constitutional monarchy faces a crisis. The elected Prime Minister proposes a law restricting press freedom, citing national security. The monarch privately expresses concern but has no constitutional power to veto the law. Civil society groups protest, and the independent judiciary reviews the law’s constitutionality. (i) What defines this country as a ‘constitutional’ monarchy? (ii) Which fundamental democratic principle is potentially threatened by the proposed law? (iii) Evaluate the role of the independent judiciary and civil society in this scenario as safeguards for democracy.
items.answer:  (i) The monarch’s powers are limited by the constitution; real legislative and executive power lies with the elected parliament and the government accountable to it, not the hereditary monarch. (ii) The fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression, specifically the freedom of the press, is threatened. (iii) The independent judiciary acts as a crucial check by reviewing the law’s constitutionality against fundamental rights. Civil society protests raise public awareness and pressure the government, demonstrating citizens’ role in defending democratic principles even when formal power structures are challenged.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Following a military coup, a country is ruled by a General who suspends the constitution, dissolves parliament, bans political opposition, and controls all media. He claims this is necessary to restore order and economic prosperity, promising elections later but setting no date. (i) What type of government does this scenario describe? (ii) Identify three democratic principles or institutions that have been violated or removed. (iii) Evaluate the General’s claim that suspending democracy is necessary for order and prosperity.
items.answer:  (i) This describes a military dictatorship, where power is seized and held by force by a military leader or group, overriding democratic institutions. (ii) Violations include : representative participation (parliament dissolved), rule of law (constitution suspended), freedom of speech/assembly (opposition banned, media controlled), and likely accountability (no elections planned). (iii) This claim is often used by dictators but is highly questionable. While dictatorships might impose superficial order through force, they typically suppress rights, lack accountability, foster corruption, and often lead to long-term instability and economic problems rather than sustainable prosperity for all.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What is a ‘Constitution’ in the context of a nation? laws

options.label: A
options.text: A historical account of all its past rulers

options.label: B
options.text: A document laying down basic principles

options.label: C
options.text: A collection of all national songs, poems

options.label: D
options.text: An annual report on the nation’s economy

items.answer:  (B) A document laying down basic principles, laws A Constitution is a fundamental document that outlines a nation’s basic principles, laws, and the framework for its government. It defines how the country will be governed and the rights of its citizens.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Why is the original manuscript of the Indian Constitution preserved in a helium-filled glass case in Parliament?

options.label: A
options.text: To make it easily accessible for daily

options.label: B
options.text: To protect it from damage, ensure longevity

options.label: C
options.text: To display it prominently during sessions

options.label: D
options.text: To allow easy modifications to its text

items.answer:  (B) To protect it from damage, ensure longevity Helium is an inert gas that does not react with paper or ink. Storing the original Constitution in a helium-filled case helps protect this invaluable document from deterioration and ensures its preservation for future generations.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: What does a Constitution primarily lay out regarding a nation’s government?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the list of national holidays yearly

options.label: B
options.text: The detailed biographies of all leaders

options.label: C
options.text: The framework of government organs, roles

options.label: D
options.text: The specific designs for currency notes

items.answer:  (C) The framework of government organs, roles A Constitution establishes the structure of the government, defining its different organs (like legislature, executive, judiciary), their respective roles, responsibilities, and the relationships between them, ensuring a systematic approach to governance.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: Who was the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the Indian Constitution?
items.answer:  (D) Dr. Rajendra Prasad Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who later became the first President of India, served as the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly, the body responsible for drafting the Indian Constitution.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: How does a Fundamental Right differ from a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: Rights are for government; DPSP for citizens

options.label: B
options.text: Rights are optional; DPSP are mandatory

options.label: C
options.text: Rights are enforceable; DPSP are guidelines

options.label: D
options.text: Rights are temporary; DPSP are permanent

items.answer:  (C) Rights are enforceable; DPSP are guidelines Fundamental Rights are legally enforceable promises to citizens, meaning one can approach a court if they are violated. Directive Principles are guidelines or goals for the government to strive for, but not directly enforceable in court.

items.chapter: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
items.stem: The Indian Constitution being a ‘living document’ implies what characteristic?

options.label: A
options.text: It is handwritten and cannot be printed

options.label: B
options.text: It can be amended or changed over time

options.label: C
options.text: It applies only to living citizens today

options.label: D
options.text: It is stored in a special biological case

items.answer:  (B) It can be amended or changed over time Referring to the Constitution as a ‘living document’ means it is not static but can be amended and adapted to meet the changing needs, aspirations, and circumstances of society over time through a defined process.
